chief_complaint: progressive headache, confusion, and right arm clumsiness over 3 weeks following a minor fall
hpi_details: 81-year-old male brought in by his concerned daughter due to a 3-week history of fluctuating confusion, memory lapses, progressive dull headaches, and increased daytime sleepiness. Over the past 5 days, daughter noticed he is dragging his right foot slightly and his right hand has become clumsy when dropping his teacup. Recalls that 4 weeks ago, he tripped over a rug at home and struck the left side of his forehead against a wooden doorpost; he had a minor bruise but did not lose consciousness and did not seek medical attention at the time. Takes warfarin for atrial fibrillation.
ideas: daughter thinks his old age and dementia are rapidly worsening after his trip
concerns: daughter is worried he had a major stroke or brain bleed because he takes warfarin
expectations: wants an emergency brain CT scan and reversal of blood thinners to stop internal bleeding
pmh: paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, type 2 diabetes mellitus, benign prostatic hyperplasia, mild age-related cognitive decline
medications: warfarin 4mg OD (recent INR measured at 3.8 last week), metformin 500mg BD, tamsulosin 400mcg OD
social_hx: ex-smoker, zero alcohol, lives alone with daughter visiting daily, previously independent

investigation_events.title: Emergency CT and anticoagulation assessment
investigation_events.availability_message: Emergency CT and coagulation results are now available. Warfarin reversal and neurosurgical transfer should proceed immediately.

results.value: Large mixed-density crescentic left frontoparietal extra-axial collection crossing suture lines, with 9 mm rightward midline shift and left lateral ventricular effacement

clinical_knowledge.topic: Subacute/Chronic Subdural Hematoma evaluation and management
core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Subacute/Chronic Subdural Hematoma is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.

Standard management emphasizes Neurosurgical emergency: immediate referral and transfer to neurosurgery for urgent surgical evacuation via burr hole drainage or craniotomy under local/general anaesthesia, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: progressive headache, confusion, and right arm clumsiness over 3 weeks following a minor fall

Key HPI features: 81-year-old male brought in by his concerned daughter due to a 3-week history of fluctuating confusion, memory lapses, progressive dull headaches, and increased daytime sleepiness. Over the past 5 days, daughter noticed he is dragging his right foot slightly and his right hand has become clumsy when dropping his teacup. Recalls that 4 weeks ago, he tripped over a rug at home and struck the left side of his forehead against a wooden doorpost; he had a minor bruise but did not lose consciousness and did not seek medical attention at the time. Takes warfarin for atrial fibrillation.

Objective/Exam findings: Neurological exam: drowsy but rousable (GCS 14: E4 V4 M6), mild right facial weakness, right upper and lower limb pronator drift and weakness (power 4/5), brisk right tendon reflexes with positive right Babinski sign. Check pupils (if left pupil dilated and sluggish -> impending uncal herniation). Vitals: check for Cushing's triad (hypertension and bradycardia indicating critical raised ICP). Bloods: urgent coagulation profile (check INR), FBC, U&Es, group and save/cross-match. Immediate emergency non-contrast CT Brain: shows crescent-shaped, hypodense or mixed-density (isodense/hypodense) extra-axial collection over the left cerebral hemisphere crossing cranial suture lines, causing significant midline shift to the right and effacement of the left lateral ventricle.
Relevant background/PMH: paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, type 2 diabetes mellitus, benign prostatic hyperplasia, mild age-related cognitive decline
Current medications: warfarin 4mg OD (recent INR measured at 3.8 last week), metformin 500mg BD, tamsulosin 400mcg OD
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Subacute/Chronic Subdural Hematoma.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Acute ischemic stroke without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Warfarin use with any head trauma, even minor — needs urgent reversal before neurosurgical intervention.
management_principles: Neurosurgical emergency: immediate referral and transfer to neurosurgery for urgent surgical evacuation via burr hole drainage or craniotomy under local/general anaesthesia
For confirmed intracranial bleeding, urgently reverse warfarin according to local protocol with IV 4-factor Prothrombin Complex Concentrate plus IV vitamin K before neurosurgical intervention.
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

reference_soap.subjective: 81M on warfarin presents with insidious 3-week fluctuating confusion, headache, and progressive right hemiparesis following a minor head trauma 4 weeks prior.
reference_soap.objective: Neurological exam: drowsy but rousable (GCS 14: E4 V4 M6), mild right facial weakness, right upper and lower limb pronator drift and weakness (power 4/5), brisk right tendon reflexes with positive right Babinski sign. Check pupils (if left pupil dilated and sluggish -> impending uncal herniation). Vitals: check for Cushing's triad (hypertension and bradycardia indicating critical raised ICP). Bloods: urgent coagulation profile (check INR), FBC, U&Es, group and save/cross-match. Immediate emergency non-contrast CT Brain: shows crescent-shaped, hypodense or mixed-density (isodense/hypodense) extra-axial collection over the left cerebral hemisphere crossing cranial suture lines, causing significant midline shift to the right and effacement of the left lateral ventricle.
reference_soap.assessment: Subacute/Chronic Subdural Haematoma (cSDH) over the left cerebral hemisphere with mass effect, precipitated by minor head trauma and warfarin anticoagulation. DDx: acute ischaemic stroke / cerebral infarct, intracranial tumour with vasogenic oedema, cerebral abscess, normal pressure hydrocephalus.
reference_soap.plan: Neurosurgical emergency: immediate referral and transfer to neurosurgery for urgent surgical evacuation via burr hole drainage or craniotomy under local/general anaesthesia. Immediate emergency reversal of warfarin anticoagulation: administer IV 4-factor Prothrombin Complex Concentrate (PCC - Beriplex/Octaplex 25-50 units/kg) plus IV Vitamin K 10mg slowly to target INR <1.5 before neurosurgical intervention (PCC reverses INR within 15 minutes, far superior to Fresh Frozen Plasma). Keep head elevated 30 degrees, monitor neurological observations (GCS/pupils) every 30 minutes.

learning_objectives: Link minor, easily forgotten head trauma in elderly or anticoagulated patients with delayed subacute/chronic subdural haematoma weeks later
Interpret CT brain findings of chronic subdural haematoma: crescent-shaped extra-axial collection crossing sutures with midline shift
Execute immediate life-saving warfarin reversal using 4-factor Prothrombin Complex Concentrate (PCC) and IV Vitamin K prior to neurosurgery
Perform serial neurological assessments monitoring GCS, pupillary symmetry, and motor signs to catch early brain herniation

teaching.one_liner: A slow venous bleed under the skull, often from a trivial head bump weeks earlier in an elderly patient on blood thinners, causing gradually worsening confusion and one-sided weakness that can look like dementia progressing.
red_flags: Warfarin use with any head trauma, even minor, requires urgent clinical assessment for intracranial bleeding

must_ask.say: Did he hit his head at any point in the past month, even a minor bump?
Is he taking warfarin or another blood thinner?
How has his confusion and arm clumsiness changed over the past weeks?
Has he been more drowsy or sleepy during the day than usual?
Which side is weaker, and when did you first notice it?
